notes:
• Fixed - a test of the Shelf's album view failed now and then on a busy machine ("the view ends at the bar"): it measured the view a fixed 0.6 s after the album was up, and the view unfolds out of its case for 0.7 s, so a quick album or a slow moment measured it mid-way. It is measured once its unfolding is over (item 343)
• Fixed - an artist's page could keep saying who another act of the same name was after the server had found the right one (Airbag from Norway still "Band · Spain · since 1998" while the Artists wall had their picture): the app kept a page for fifteen minutes and asked nothing of it again in that time, and the server, while it looked the act up again, answered with the other act's entry. Who they are is now asked at every visit, and asked again every few seconds while the server is still looking, in the app and on the page; meanwhile the server no longer says the other act (item 342)
• Fixed - the Library Scanner kept saying "MusicBrainz isn't answering; trying again in a few minutes" and stopped identifying ten minutes at a time, over and over: the lookup of each match's act (item 333) asked MusicBrainz for matches iTunes had made ("Ask iTunes too", an id MusicBrainz has no release for), MusicBrainz refused each (HTTP 400), and three refusals in a row were taken for MusicBrainz being away; nothing kept them as asked, so the same albums were asked again at every turn. A match of iTunes's is not asked of MusicBrainz, and a release MusicBrainz refuses or doesn't know is kept as asked, once, and never taken for MusicBrainz away (item 341)
• Fixed - an artist's page said who another act of the same name was: the owner's nine albums by Airbag from Norway showed "Band · Spain · since 1998" and the Spanish band's picture and links. Who an act is was looked up once on MusicBrainz by the name alone (the first Airbag it found) and kept for the name. The page and the background lookups now take the act the library's albums are by: the MusicBrainz id their tags or matches say, else the act MusicBrainz credits with their titles; one kept for the name that is another act is looked up again by itself. Acts that share a name in the library (item 330) are each looked up and pictured as themselves, on their page and on the Artists wall (item 340)
• Fixed - the Android app's Library wall lost a sort chosen there ("Recently added" back to "Release date") once an album or Now playing had been opened over it and closed: the wall was built again in the view it had been opened with. Its sort, Focus, filter and room are now kept through whatever is opened over it, and its filter no longer comes back or goes (item 339)
• Improved - the share card is the card alone: its review is always on it, a fifth bigger (26 to 31 px, the card growing to hold it), with whose words they are as before; "If you like this" (the three acts suggested under it), the places to hear or read about the record and Settings → Setup → Share Card (the Review switch, the services and their default, the review sites) are gone, from the page and the app, with all that made them: the server's suggestions, its search links, its Qobuz app link and the settings kept for them (item 336)
• Fixed - the Android app's Library wall came back narrowed to the last name typed in its filter ("airbag": 34 of 13,917 albums), with no field to see or clear it: the app kept the name filter with the wall's sort and Focus, for the next visit and the next start, where the page keeps it for the moment only. The filter is no longer kept (one kept already is let go), and a wall opened with a filter shows it in its field (item 338)
• Fixed - queuing an album while another played stopped the one playing, where Mandarin made it as it played (DSD from PCM, upsampling, an album as one stream): queuing told the making to keep only the queued album's tracks, and the stream the device was playing was stopped, the device falling silent mid-track. Queuing now stops nothing; playing an album at once, or skipping, still stops what is no longer wanted, but never what a device is still to play (item 337)
• Fixed - the MusicBrainz lookup that files albums under their act (item 333) read the whole library again, and wrote the album edits' backup (covers included), for every album it filed, every few seconds through a whole library; filing an album is no edit: the library is now read again once a minute at most while it works, and once it is done, the backup left alone (item 335)
• Improved - logging is on by default, in the server and in the Android app (Settings → Setup → Logging): a fault seen once is in the log when it is saved, where it was off unless switched on, and an app installed again (a test build over a release) started with it off. Switched off it stays off, across restarts and updates; each log is kept to a few megabytes, without what is yours alone, as before (item 334)
• New - two acts of one name are told apart by Mandarin's own MusicBrainz matches too, where the files carry no MusicBrainz id: an album identified before item 330 kept its release but not the act's id, so each such applied match's release is asked of musicbrainz.org once (the pack keeps the act's name alone), the act's id and MusicBrainz's word for it kept, and the album filed under that act at once, no file touched. Names with the most albums go first (a name with one album is never two acts); it takes turns with identifying new albums and keeps to the identification scan's hours. Albums never identified still need their files tagged, or the artist renamed on their page (item 333)
• Fixed - a track Mandarin stopped making on purpose (another album played, or skipped from while it waited its turn) was logged as "transcode failed … another play", though nothing failed; it is now logged as stopped, with why ("no longer made: skipped from"). It also failed dev's test run on a slower machine, where the earlier track was still waiting its turn (item 332)
• Improved - the signal path in as few steps as it can be: Source ("FLAC 16-bit 44.1 kHz 2ch"); Bit depth conversion ("16-bit to 64-bit float"), where Mandarin works the samples (upsampling, DSD made from PCM, the DSP: it decodes them to 64-bit float and works them there; a stream it only passes on has no such step); Volume levelling where it is on ("−7.3 dB · ReplayGain"); then what goes out in one line ("Gaussian steep ×16 · 7th-order · DSD256", "Long ×2 · 24/88.2 kHz", the dither with it where Mandarin makes it), where upsampling, the DSD modulator and the output were three; and the device's own word on what its DAC is fed, as before. Now playing's line under the title is that same short line (item 331)
• Fixed - two acts of the same name (Airbag from Norway and Airbag from Argentina) were one artist, their albums run together on the Artists wall, the artist's page and "More by". Every album is now filed under an artist of its own in the library (an artists table, each act its own id, the same name allowed on many), told by the act's MusicBrainz id: from the files' tags (MusicBrainz Album Artist Id, else Artist Id, as Picard writes them in FLAC, MP3, M4A and the rest), else from the album's applied MusicBrainz match. Acts that share a name are each their own artist on the wall, in search and on their page, each told apart by MusicBrainz's word for it (from a match) or its albums' years; an album's link to its artist and its "More by" open its own act, on the page and in the app. A name only one act has stays one artist, its tagged and untagged albums together. The next scan reads every file's tags once more for the id (item 330)
